preview.headline: Flyers Visit Senators in Clash of Possession and Chance Generation
preview.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers travel to face the Ottawa Senators on November 19, 2026, looking to avenge an earlier 3-1 defeat from October 17. Both teams enter on identical rest with one full calendar day off, though the Flyers are navigating a heavier recent schedule with three games in the last seven days.
preview.away_analysis: The Flyers boast elite underlying metrics, ranking 4th in expected goals percentage (56.01%) and 2nd in high-danger chances percentage (57.38%). However, their actual goal share sits at just 49.02% due to a 20th-ranked shooting percentage of 9.03% and a struggling 29th-ranked power play. Despite strong defensive suppression ranking 3rd in expected goals against per 60, Vladar enters with a lower recent GSAx rank of 58.
preview.home_analysis: The Senators ride a three-game winning streak into this matchup, backed by strong possession metrics that rank 2nd in both Corsi For % and Corsi For per 60. Ottawa is converting its chances effectively, boasting the 6th-best shooting percentage in the league to fuel a 4th-ranked goals for percentage. Like the Flyers, the Senators struggle with special teams, ranking 32nd on the power play and 19th on the penalty kill.
matchup_edges: Philadelphia holds a major edge in high-danger chance generation, ranking 2nd in HDCF% compared to Ottawa at 17th.
Ottawa controls the flow of play much better through sheer volume, ranking 2nd in Corsi For % compared to Philadelphia at 11th.
The Senators have capitalized on their opportunities much more efficiently, sitting 6th in shooting percentage while the Flyers rank 20th.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, as both squads feature bottom-tier power plays that could neutralize each other if the game turns into a parade to the penalty box.
preview.key_question: Can the Flyers' elite expected-goal generation finally translate to finish against Ottawa, or will the Senators' superior shooting efficiency carry them to another win?
preview.quick_takeaway: Philadelphia dominates the high-danger metrics, but Ottawa's superior finishing and possession volume create a fascinating test of process versus results.

preview.headline: Islanders Edge Jets on Power‑Play Efficiency
preview.summary: The New York Islanders, riding a three‑game winning streak, will look to leverage their superior power‑play conversion and defensive discipline against a struggling Winnipeg Jets team that has faltered on the penalty kill. The matchup hinges on the Islanders’ high‑danger chance generation versus the Jets’ ability to capitalize on their power‑play advantage.
preview.away_analysis: The Islanders’ 18.33% power‑play rate ranks 26th, but their 85.94% penalty kill—fourth best—shows defensive resilience. With a Corsi For % of 47.69 (27th) and high‑danger chance share of 49.82% (18th), they generate quality opportunities but struggle to convert expected goals into shots (xGF% 48.77 vs GF% 50.91). Sorokin’s strong GSAx rank (4) suggests a reliable netminder to support the team’s short‑stint defensive effort.
preview.home_analysis: The Jets’ power play at 23.88% (11th) is their standout asset, yet their 71.88% kill (25th) is a glaring weakness. Their Corsi For % of 48.60 (23rd) and low expected goals per 60 (2.27, 26th) indicate limited offensive pressure. Daws’ GSAx rank of 45 implies a less consistent goaltender, raising concerns when the Jets face a disciplined penalty‑kill squad.
matchup_edges: Islanders’ 85.94% penalty kill outmatches Jets’ 71.88% kill
Islanders’ higher high‑danger chance share (49.82% vs 45.1%) gives them more quality scoring opportunities
Jets’ superior power‑play rate (23.88% vs 18.33%) could offset defensive lapses
preview.x_factor: The key will be whether the Jets can turn their power‑play advantage into a decisive goal before the Islanders’ defensive discipline neutralizes their short‑stint offense.
preview.key_question: Will the Jets’ power‑play edge translate into a win, or will the Islanders’ penalty‑kill prowess and goaltending depth keep the game in reach?
preview.quick_takeaway: Islanders’ defensive strength and goaltending depth give them the edge, but Jets’ potent power play could swing the game.

preview.headline: Well-Rested Hurricanes Host Fatigue-Ridden Canadiens
preview.summary: The red-hot Carolina Hurricanes return home with four days of rest to host a Montreal Canadiens squad playing its fourth game in seven days and finishing a back-to-back set.
preview.away_analysis: The Canadiens arrive with severe fatigue concerns, playing their fourth game in seven days with zero days of rest. While Montreal ranks 3rd in both Goals For % and shooting percentage, their underlying metrics point toward regression, sitting 26th in expected goals percentage and 28th in expected goals against per 60. Dobes projects to get the nod in net, holding a 72nd-ranked GSAx over his last 20 appearances.
preview.home_analysis: The Hurricanes are firing on all cylinders, boasting a four-game win streak while leading the NHL in Corsi For %, expected goals percentage, high-danger chance share, and actual goals percentage. Carolina dominates play territorially, ranking 1st in both shot-attempt generation and suppression, while maintaining elite special teams anchored by a top-four penalty kill and a top-ten power play. Kochetkov anchors the back end with strong form, ranking 7th in GSAx over his last 20 games.
matchup_edges: Territorial dominance: Carolina leads the league in Corsi For %, expected goals percentage, and high-danger chance share.
Schedule and rest: The Hurricanes enjoy four days of rest compared to Montreal playing their fourth game in seven days on zero rest.
Special teams: Carolina holds a distinct advantage with a top-ten power play and elite penalty kill against a weak Montreal power play.
preview.x_factor: Can Montreal's high shooting percentage withstand Carolina's league-leading defensive suppression, or will the tired legs of the Canadiens buckle under the Hurricanes' relentless forecheck?
preview.key_question: Can Dobes and the Canadiens defense survive a barrage of shots from a fully rested Carolina offense that dominates possession?
preview.quick_takeaway: Carolina's overwhelming territorial dominance and massive rest advantage create a daunting matchup for a fatigued Montreal squad.

preview.headline: Sabres and Capitals Clash Looking to Snap Skids
preview.summary: The Buffalo Sabres travel to Washington to face the Capitals on November 19, 2026, with both teams looking to break out of current losing streaks. The Sabres bring a five-game skid into the matchup, while the Capitals are looking to bounce back from three straight losses. Both squads enter on identical rest with one day off following a matching three-game workload over the last week.
preview.away_analysis: The Sabres control play well at 5-on-5, ranking 7th in Corsi For percentage and 12th in shot attempts per 60, but they struggle to finish their chances. Their 8.76% shooting percentage ranks 22nd in the league, dragging down their actual goals percentage despite respectable underlying expected-goal numbers. Special teams remain a glaring weakness, with both the power play and penalty kill sitting near the bottom of the league.
preview.home_analysis: The Capitals hold a distinct territorial advantage, ranking 4th in Corsi For percentage and 3rd in shot generation per 60 minutes. Washington also wins the high-danger battle more consistently than Buffalo, sitting 11th in high-danger chance share compared to the Sabres' 22nd-ranked mark. While their special teams units are also outside the league's upper tier, their efficient 10.08% shooting percentage gives them a sharper finishing edge.
matchup_edges: Washington holds a significant edge in high-danger chance share, ranking 11th compared to Buffalo's 22nd-ranked mark.
The Capitals generate sustained offensive pressure much more frequently, sitting 3rd in shot-attempt generation per 60.
Buffalo suppresses shot volume effectively, ranking 4th in Corsi Against per 60 to counter Washington's attack.
preview.x_factor: Special teams efficiency could decide a tight game, as both teams struggle heavily on the penalty kill and rank in the bottom tier of the league.
preview.key_question: Can the Sabres find a way to convert their territorial play into actual goals against a Capitals team that dominates possession?
preview.quick_takeaway: Washington's superior high-danger chance generation gives them the edge, but both struggling teams desperately need a defensive spark to break their skids.

preview.headline: Kings Visit Struggling Maple Leafs Looking to Expose Special Teams Weakness
preview.summary: The Los Angeles Kings travel to face the Toronto Maple Leafs on November 19, 2026, with both clubs operating on a single day of rest. While the Kings have outperformed their underlying metrics to sit comfortably in actual goal share, the Maple Leafs enter this matchup desperately looking to snap a dismal seven-game losing streak.
preview.away_analysis: The Kings rely heavily on finishing efficiency and high-danger chance creation, ranking 10th in high-danger chances percentage despite sitting 20th in expected goals percentage. Their 53.49 goals-for percentage outperforms their 48.79 expected goals percentage, pointing to strong conversion rates that make up for defensive leaks. However, Los Angeles carries a glaring weakness on the penalty kill, ranking 29th in the league at 68.33 percent.
preview.home_analysis: Toronto plays a tighter defensive brand, ranking 9th in expected goals against per 60 and boasting a stellar 7th-ranked penalty kill at 83.56 percent. Their special teams are rounded out by a potent power play that ranks 7th in the NHL at 25.4 percent. Despite a modest 16th-ranked expected goals percentage, the Maple Leafs generate quality looks with a top-10 high-danger chance share.
matchup_edges: Toronto holds a massive special teams advantage, especially on a penalty kill that ranks 27 spots higher than Los Angeles.
The Maple Leafs suppress scoring chances much more effectively, ranking 9th in expected goals against per 60 compared to the Kings at 27th.
Los Angeles possesses the superior high-danger conversion game, capitalizing on a top-10 high-danger chance share to drive a top-10 goals-for percentage.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution will dictate the flow, as Toronto's top-10 power play attacks a porous Kings penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can the Maple Leafs finally break their seven-game skid by exploiting the Kings' defensive zone vulnerabilities?
preview.quick_takeaway: Toronto owns a clear special teams and defensive suppression edge, but Los Angeles brings superior finishing touch into hostile territory.

preview.headline: St. Louis Blues vs. Pittsburgh Penguins: A Battle of Possession and Discipline
preview.summary: The Blues’ superior possession and penalty kill give them a slight edge over the Penguins, who have the league‑best power play but are hampered by a weak shooting percentage and recent slump. The matchup hinges on whether the Penguins can convert their high‑danger chances into goals while the Blues stay disciplined and let their goaltender, Hofer, keep the score low.
preview.away_analysis: The Blues lead in Corsi For % (49.44, rank 18) and have a stronger CF/60 (57.41, rank 11) than Pittsburgh, indicating better puck control. Their high‑danger chances share (56.32, rank 5) and top‑tier expected goals per 60 (3.1, rank 3) suggest they’re generating quality chances, yet their shooting % (8.81, rank 21) is the league’s 21st, hinting at finishing issues. Hofer’s GSAx rank 8 keeps the Blues’ goals against in check, especially on the road.
preview.home_analysis: Pittsburgh’s Corsi For % (53.91, rank 3) and CF/60 (60.57, rank 5) outpace the Blues, showing strong possession. However, their shooting % (7.69, rank 29) is the league’s lowest, and their GF% (42.5, rank 26) lags behind the Blues’ 50.98. The Penguins’ power play is average (20.0%, rank 19) but their penalty kill (79.63%, rank 14) is weaker than the Blues’ 82.14% (rank 9). Silovs’ GSAx rank 54 suggests a shaky netminder on home ice.
matchup_edges: Blues’ superior penalty‑kill and disciplined play give them a small advantage over Pittsburgh’s weaker penalty kill
Blues generate higher quality chances per 60 (3.1 vs. 2.88) despite similar expected goal percentages
Pittsburgh’s stronger possession metrics (Corsi For % and CF/60) could offset the Blues’ shooting inefficiency
preview.x_factor: The game will test whether Pittsburgh can translate their possession advantage into goals against a disciplined Blues defense and a goaltender who’s performed well over the last 20 games.
preview.key_question: Will the Penguins’ ability to control the puck compensate for their low shooting percentage and recent slump, or will the Blues’ disciplined defense and strong penalty kill keep the score tight?
preview.quick_takeaway: Blues’ disciplined play and better penalty kill give them the edge, but Pittsburgh’s possession advantage means the game could tilt on a single conversion.

preview.headline: Hot-Streak Oilers Visit Dominant Lightning Squad
preview.summary: The Edmonton Oilers bring a six-game winning streak into Tampa Bay to face a Lightning team boasting elite underlying metrics and league-leading finishing talent. While Edmonton relies on a lethal power play to mask poor territorial control, Tampa Bay controls the pace of play with top-tier possession and expected goal numbers.
preview.away_analysis: Despite riding a six-game winning streak, the Oilers struggle heavily to control play at 5-on-5, ranking 28th in Corsi For% (46.97%) and expected goals share. Their offensive generation sits near the bottom of the league with an expected goals for per 60 rate of 2.15, forcing them to heavily lean on an elite power play clicking at 35.06% (2nd).
preview.home_analysis: The Lightning represent a complete statistical powerhouse, ranking in the top five for Corsi For%, expected goals percentage, and defensive suppression. They also boast the league's top-ranked shooting percentage at 13.79%, though their 24th-ranked penalty kill remains a notable vulnerability against Edmonton's dangerous special teams.
matchup_edges: Tampa Bay holds a massive 5-on-5 territorial advantage, ranking 5th in expected goals percentage compared to Edmonton at 28th.
Edmonton features a lethal power play ranked 2nd in the league, while Tampa Bay struggles on the penalty kill at 24th.
The Lightning dominate high-danger chance creation, ranking 6th in high-danger chances percentage against an Oilers squad ranking 28th.
preview.x_factor: Special teams efficiency will dictate momentum, as Edmonton's elite power play matches up directly against Tampa Bay's suspect penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can the Oilers sustain their winning streak by finishing opportunistically, or will the Lightning's dominant 5-on-5 play overwhelm them?
preview.quick_takeaway: Tampa Bay owns a massive territorial and 5-on-5 advantage, but Edmonton's scorching-hot power play gives them a puncher's chance if the game gets undisciplined.

preview.headline: Blue Jackets vs. Blackhawks: Possession‑Heavy Blue Jackets Face a Resurgent Home Team
preview.summary: The Blue Jackets, despite a five‑game slide, dominate the puck with a 51.58 % Corsi and a solid 57.9 Corsi/60. Chicago’s offense is comparatively weaker, but their penalty‑kill (79.1 %) and high shooting percentage (9.68 %) give them a defensive edge. The game hinges on whether the Jackets’ possession can translate into goals or the Blackhawks’ disciplined defense and efficient power play will keep the score low.
preview.away_analysis: Blue’s 51.58 % Corsi and 57.9 Corsi/60 place them in the league’s top 10 for possession, yet their 40 % Goals % and 6.72 % shooting lag behind. Their expected‑goal advantage (47.31 % vs. 43.12 %) suggests they’re generating more quality chances, but finishing has been inconsistent. A 3.27 penalties/60 rate keeps the team from capitalizing on their possession advantage.
preview.home_analysis: Chicago’s 45.67 % Corsi and 46.9 Corsi/60 rank near the bottom, reflecting a struggle to control the puck. However, their 9.68 % shooting and 79.1 % penalty kill provide a defensive backbone. The Blackhawks’ expected‑goal numbers (43.12 % vs. 47.31 %) are slightly lower, but their higher shooting efficiency and strong kill could offset possession deficits.
matchup_edges: Blue’s possession edge vs. Chicago’s defensive discipline
Blackhawks’ higher shooting % and penalty kill vs. Blue’s finishing woes
Blue’s 62nd GSAx rank vs. Chicago’s 52nd indicates a marginal goalie advantage for the home team
preview.x_factor: The key X‑factor is whether Blue’s possession advantage will overcome their shooting slump, or if Chicago’s efficient penalty kill and high shooting % will keep the game tight.
preview.key_question: Can the Blue Jackets convert their possession advantage into a winning goal against a Blackhawks team that relies on disciplined defense and a sharp penalty kill?
preview.quick_takeaway: Blue’s puck control will be the deciding factor, but Chicago’s defensive grit and efficient shooting could keep the score close.

preview.headline: Wild’s Power‑Play Edge Faces Flames’ Defensive Stamina
preview.summary: The Minnesota Wild enter the game on a four‑game winning streak, powered by a league‑best power‑play and top‑tier finishing. Calgary, meanwhile, is riding a single win but has shown resilience on the penalty kill, though its shooting is a league‑bottom concern. The matchup will hinge on whether the Wild can convert their high‑danger chances into goals or the Flames can blunt that with a disciplined defense and a shutout‑prone goaltender.
preview.away_analysis: The Wild’s 25.61% power‑play ranks sixth, and their 12.21% shooting is fourth in the league, indicating a potent finishing ability. Their Corsi For % sits near the middle of the pack, but their 51.16% high‑danger chances and 69.81% goals‑for rank 2 suggest they generate quality scoring opportunities. Wallstedt, ranked #1 in GSAx, is a strong defensive anchor for a team that has a solid penalty kill at 80% (rank 13).
preview.home_analysis: Calgary’s 27.45% power‑play is the fourth‑best, and their penalty kill is elite at 82.35% (rank 8). However, their shooting at 7.88% (rank 28) and goals‑for rank 21 reflect a struggle to finish chances. Wolf’s GSAx rank 67 shows a less reliable net‑minder, but the Flames’ defensive suppression (expected‑goals‑against 2.55 per 60, rank 14) can offset the Wild’s high‑danger output.
matchup_edges: Wild’s high‑danger chances (51.16%) vs. Flames’ strong penalty kill (82.35%)
Wild’s elite power‑play (25.61%) vs. Flames’ slightly better power‑play (27.45%)
Wild’s top‑tier shooter (12.21% shooting) vs. Flames’ low shooting (7.88%)
preview.x_factor: The Wild’s ability to translate high‑danger chances into goals will be tested by Calgary’s disciplined defense and a goaltender who has struggled in recent games.
preview.key_question: Can the Wild’s prolific power‑play and finishing outpace Calgary’s defensive resilience and penalty‑kill prowess?
preview.quick_takeaway: Wild’s high‑danger chances and power‑play advantage could give them the edge, but Calgary’s defensive discipline and elite penalty kill make for a tight, disciplined battle.

preview.headline: Avalanche’s possession edge may keep Ducks on the defensive
preview.summary: The Avalanche have a clear advantage in possession, generating more shots and high‑danger chances than the Ducks, while the Ducks’ power‑play efficiency remains the only bright spot in their game plan. Both teams are coming off a loss and have similar recent workloads, but the Avalanche’s stronger offensive output and better penalty‑kill will likely tilt the balance.
preview.away_analysis: The Ducks are struggling to maintain possession, with a 49.22% Corsi For and 54.81 CF/60, placing them 21st and 20th in the league. Their power play is elite (36.0% PP, 1st) but their penalty kill is sub‑par (74.7%, 21st). Offensively, their shooting percentage is high (11.99%, 5th), suggesting good finish, yet their expected‑goals metrics lag (44.33% xGF, 27th).
preview.home_analysis: Colorado dominates possession (52.81% CF, 62.37 CF/60, 6th) and produces more expected goals (49.26%, 19th). Their high‑danger chance share (46.85%, 24th) and solid penalty kill (80.88%, 11th) give them a defensive edge. Their shooting percentage is lower (9.73%, 13th) but their expected‑goals per 60 (2.58) is competitive, indicating efficient conversion of chances.
matchup_edges: Colorado’s CF/60 advantage gives them more shot opportunities per minute
Ducks’ power‑play efficiency is the only real threat to Avalanche’s defense
Avalanche’s better penalty kill reduces Ducks’ chances to capitalize on penalties
preview.x_factor: The Ducks’ power play is the only tool that could offset Colorado’s possession advantage; if it stays above 35%, the game could be tighter than the stats suggest.
preview.key_question: Can the Ducks’ elite power play overcome Colorado’s superior possession and penalty‑kill to force a closer contest?
preview.quick_takeaway: Colorado’s possession and defensive strengths give them the edge, but the Ducks’ power play could keep the score close.

preview.headline: Canucks Edge Kraken in a Battle of High‑Danger Chances
preview.summary: The Canucks, riding a two‑game win streak and a solid 45.79% Corsi advantage, will test the Kraken’s defensive depth in a matchup where both teams generate similar high‑danger chances but the Canucks have a higher shooting percentage. With the Kraken on a three‑game slide and the Canucks’ goalie ranked 49th in recent GSAx, the game hinges on the Canucks’ ability to convert their 41.22% high‑danger share into goals while the Kraken will look to exploit the Canucks’ 63.16% penalty‑kill weakness.
preview.away_analysis: Vancouver’s 45.79% Corsi for and 41.22% high‑danger chances give them a possession edge, while their 9.46% shooting percentage—ranked 15th—suggests efficient finishing. Their 63.16% penalty kill is the league’s 31st best, so any Kraken penalty could be costly. The Canucks’ recent two‑game win streak and 2‑day rest will help keep their offense sharp.
preview.home_analysis: Seattle’s 44.12% goals for and 38.71% high‑danger chances show a competitive offense, but their 67.16 Corsi against per 60 and 62.74% penalty kill rank 32nd, indicating defensive struggles. The Kraken’s 4‑day rest and 2‑game win in the last 7 days could give them a rhythm, but their recent 3‑game losing streak may dampen confidence. Grubauer’s GSAx rank of 38th suggests a solid but not elite performance.
matchup_edges: Canucks’ possession advantage (45.79% Corsi) vs Kraken’s weaker 40.07% Corsi
Canucks’ higher shooting percentage (9.46%) vs Kraken’s 9.38%
Kraken’s penalty‑kill weakness (63.16%) could expose Canucks’ power‑play opportunities
preview.x_factor: The Canucks’ high‑danger share (41.22%) paired with their efficient shooting makes them poised to outscore the Kraken, whose defense struggles to suppress shot attempts and whose penalty kill is the league’s 31st best.
preview.key_question: Can the Canucks’ possession edge and shooting efficiency translate into a win against a Kraken side that has been on a three‑game slide and has a weak penalty kill?
preview.quick_takeaway: Canucks’ possession and shooting advantage could tip the scales against a Kraken team struggling defensively and on the penalty kill.

preview.headline: Stars’ Power‑Play Edge vs Knights’ Penalty‑Kill Prowess
preview.summary: The Dallas Stars are riding a three‑game win streak and boast a league‑best 23.53% power‑play, while Vegas is battling a three‑game losing streak and has a solid 77.59% kill. The Stars’ possession advantage (Corsi 51.21%) and high‑danger share (56.46%) give them a clear edge over the Knights’ 48.38% Corsi and 51.93% high‑danger share. However, Vegas’ 89.19% penalty‑kill and better expected‑goals‑against per 60 (1.92 vs 2.53) suggest the Knights could shut down the Stars’ offense if the game stays tight.
preview.away_analysis: Dallas’s 51.21% Corsi and 58.65% expected‑goals percentage make them the more dominant possession team, and their high‑danger share (56.46%) is the fourth‑best in the league. The Stars’ power‑play (23.53%) ranks twelfth, but their penalty‑kill (89.19%) is the second‑best, keeping the Knights’ opportunities limited. Oettinger’s 9th‑ranked GSAX over the last 20 games shows a reliable netminder for the Stars.
preview.home_analysis: Vegas struggles with a three‑game losing streak and sits near the bottom of the league in Corsi (48.38%) and shooting (7.22%). Their power‑play is elite (26.76%, 5th overall), but the penalty‑kill (77.59%) is only 18th. The Knights’ expected‑goals‑against per 60 (2.53) is higher than Dallas’s 1.92, meaning the Stars’ offense could be more effective.
matchup_edges: Stars’ superior possession (Corsi 51.21% vs 48.38%)
Stars’ league‑best penalty‑kill (89.19% vs 77.59%)
Knights’ elite power‑play (26.76%) gives them a potential swing if the Stars’ defense falters
preview.x_factor: The key will be whether Dallas can keep Vegas’ high‑danger chances in check; the Stars’ 56.46% share of high‑danger opportunities is the best in the league, but Vegas’ 89.19% kill could neutralize that advantage if the game stays close.
preview.key_question: Will Dallas’ possession advantage translate into a win, or will Vegas’ elite power‑play and strong penalty‑kill swing the game in their favor?
preview.quick_takeaway: Stars’ possession and penalty‑kill advantage give them the edge, but Vegas’ power‑play could turn the tide if the Stars’ defense falters.
